name: MITF (splash white)
summary: The first of two splash-white loci (with PAX3): white over the legs, belly and face, often a broad blaze and blue eyes, dominant and very variable in extent. UC Davis recognises six MITF splash variants - SW1, SW3, SW5, SW6, SW7 and SW8; SW1 is the widespread one and the rest are rare or confined to a family. SW9 is a commercial laboratory's name for a variant in the Pura Raza Espanola and is not on the UC Davis list. No horse with two copies of SW3, SW5, SW6, SW7 or SW8 has been detected; UC Davis says such pairs may be lethal as embryos and advises against breeding two SW3 carriers. No outcome is published for a pair of two different variants. Splash is two genes, so a horse can carry a copy here and a copy at PAX3 and be whiter than either alone. Some splash-white horses are deaf.

phenotypes.name: Splash white
phenotypes.description: One splash variant. Typically a broad blaze, white legs with a clean, sharply bounded edge, white on the belly and often blue eyes - but expression varies enormously: the same genotype can show no more than a star and a sock, or a great deal of white. No rule that one variant gives more white than another is established.

phenotypes.name: Bold splash white
phenotypes.description: Two copies of the same variant, where that pair is known alive. More white than one copy gives, and such a horse may be very extensively or entirely white.

phenotypes.name: Splash white, pair not documented
phenotypes.description: Two different MITF splash variants. No outcome is published for any such pair. More white than one variant gives is expected, and such a horse can be extensively white, but the exact outcome is variable and not characterised; no consistent appearance should be assumed.

phenotypes.name: Two copies, never detected
phenotypes.description: No horse with two copies of this variant has been detected. UC Davis says such homozygotes may be lethal as embryos; that is not established.

conditions.name: Deafness risk (assumption of this data)
conditions.description: Some splash-white horses, but not all, are deaf from birth: the pigment cells missing from the coat can be missing from the inner ear too. SW5 is treated here as carrying a raised risk, and so is every pair of two splash variants. That is a cautious rule of this data, not an established risk table for each genotype: UC Davis says the risk for single and combined variants still needs study, and that it is not known whether SW8 alone causes deafness.
